title: Policy: Securities Trading

tiers.name: any director of Fletcher Building Limited
tiers.description: Directors of the listed parent. Subject to the same consent regime, No Trade Periods and insider trading prohibition as every other covered person; the Policy draws no distinction between directors and other covered persons for any substantive rule.

tiers.name: all members of the Executive Committee
tiers.description: Executive Committee members. Same regime as directors; no separate clearance route or additional restriction.

tiers.name: all persons directly reporting to a member of the Executive Committee
tiers.description: Direct reports to Executive Committee members, deemed to have or have the opportunity to be in possession of material non-public information. Same regime as directors.

tiers.name: trusts, companies or other entities controlled by such before-mentioned persons
tiers.description: Controlled trusts, companies and other entities of directors, Executive Committee members and their direct reports. Paragraph 2.2 extends coverage to all interests whether direct, indirect, contingent, beneficial or legal, including interests held through trusts, associates, related parties, spouses and closely-held companies where the person can influence or control that person or entity.

tiers.name: anyone else notified as being an insider by the Company from time to time
tiers.description: Persons designated as insiders by the Company; they must give the Company Secretary written confirmation that they have received and understood the Policy.

tiers.name: any other employee, secondee, consultant, adviser or contractor in possession of material non-public information
tiers.description: Anyone else within the group who actually holds material non-public information; coverage is triggered by possession of information rather than by role.

tiers.name: Any employee who is offered participation in equity based incentive remuneration
tiers.description: The only tier with a distinct substantive rule. Clause 6 bans this tier from transactions limiting the economic risk of participating in equity based incentive remuneration. The tier is defined by the offer of participation, so it reaches employees who are not otherwise covered by the Policy's consent regime.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions (whether through the use of derivatives or otherwise) which limit the economic risk of participating in the equity based incentive remuneration

windows.end_anchor: after the annual results announcement is generally available to the market, which is usually the 3rd Wednesday in August
after the half year results announcement is generally available to the market, which is usually the 3rd Wednesday in February

windows.start_anchor: date there is management commitment to seek approval for the funds raising (non pro-rata equity raising/placement)
windows.end_anchor: the first day after market informed

windows.start_anchor: 30 days prior to release of a prospectus for a general public offer of securities
windows.end_anchor: the first day after public release

windows.start_anchor: day that there is a realistic prospect of a significant acquisition or divestment transaction arising, having regard to the group as a whole
windows.end_anchor: after full public disclosure is generally available to the market

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Fletcher Building Company Secretary (Deputy Company Secretary if unavailable) holds the discretion: 'the approval to trade is at the discretion of the Fletcher Building Company Secretary' and Schedule II is only a set of 'general guidelines on when approval will not be granted'. The event-driven No Trade Periods for capital structure changes and corporate activity are self-executing and by their nature undisclosed, and refusals are confidential because 'In declining any approval to trade, no reasons need be given.'

rules.detail: Listed derivatives over Fletcher Building securities are within the Policy's definition of both 'trade' and 'securities', so trading them requires prior written notification to and consent from the Company Secretary and is barred during No Trade Periods. There is no express derivatives clause and no outright prohibition.
rules.evidence: 'trade' includes buying or selling listed securities, or agreeing to do so, and trading in derivatives (such as options or warrants) over or which relate to Fletcher Building securities, in each case whether as principal or agent

rules.detail: The definition of 'trade' in 1.1 catches derivatives 'over or which relate to Fletcher Building securities' with no venue limit, so an OTC put and call written with a bank is a trade requiring consent. Paragraph 3.4, which lists the securities covered, is narrower and refers only to 'listed derivatives', but the consent form expressly contemplates an 'off-market trade', so OTC positions must be cleared.
rules.evidence: trading in derivatives (such as options or warrants) over or which relate to Fletcher Building securities, in each case whether as principal or agent, but it does not include subscription for, or the issue of, new securities.

rules.tier: Any employee who is offered participation in equity based incentive remuneration
rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no consent route, on any transaction (derivative or otherwise) limiting the economic risk of participating in equity based incentive remuneration. The stated purpose is that 'the incentive remains at risk until achieved', so the ban bites while awards are unvested or subject to performance hurdles.
rules.evidence: Any employee who is offered participation in equity based incentive remuneration is prohibited from entering into transactions (whether through the use of derivatives or otherwise) which limit the economic risk of participating in the equity based incentive remuneration.

rules.tier: Any employee who is offered participation in equity based incentive remuneration
rules.detail: The Policy does not name a restricted-but-vested state, but Schedule I distinguishes the acquisition of an interest under a scheme from 'the subsequent transfer of the full and unrestricted titles to the shares on the satisfaction of, and at a time fixed by, the terms of the scheme'. Until unrestricted title transfers the incentive is arguably not yet 'achieved', so the clause 6 ban should be treated as still applying.
rules.evidence: This policy also includes a prohibition from entering into transactions which limit the economic risk of participating in equity based incentive remuneration, so that the incentive remains at risk until achieved.

rules.detail: Once full and unrestricted title has passed and the incentive has been achieved, clause 6 is spent; hedging of freely held shares, and of shares never acquired through an incentive plan, is not prohibited. Any such derivative is nonetheless a 'trade' requiring prior written consent from the Company Secretary and cannot be entered during a No Trade Period.
rules.evidence: Before trading the Company's securities, persons covered by this Policy must, in writing: (a) notify the Fletcher Building Limited Company Secretary of their intention to trade in securities, and receive consent to do so

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and similar structures are not named. An agreement to sell is expressly a trade, so a forward sale or collar-plus-loan monetisation of unrestricted shares needs prior written consent, valid 10 trading days, and must be outside a No Trade Period. Monetising equity incentive awards that are still at risk would breach clause 6.
rules.evidence: 'trade' includes buying or selling listed securities, or agreeing to do so

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy or its Schedules. A short sale would still be a 'trade' requiring consent, but there is no express prohibition.
Securities lending and borrowing are not mentioned, and the definition of 'trade' (buying, selling, agreeing to do so, and trading in derivatives) does not obviously sweep in a stock loan.

CFDs are not named. A CFD is a derivative which relates to Fletcher Building securities and so is a 'trade' requiring prior written consent. If the underlying exposure is equity incentive remuneration still at risk, clause 6 prohibits it outright.
rules.evidence: trading in derivatives (such as options or warrants) over or which relate to Fletcher Building securities

rules.detail: Margin lending is not mentioned. There is no prohibition, no notification obligation and no guidance on forced sales by a margin lender during a No Trade Period.

Granting a mortgage, charge, lien or pledge over Fletcher Building securities is not mentioned and is not within the definition of 'trade', which is confined to buying, selling, agreeing to do so and trading in derivatives.

Secured financing in respect of Fletcher Building securities is not addressed at all: no prohibition, no clearance requirement, no disclosure trigger. The loan leg of a funded collar is therefore not caught by the Policy, though the security granted must not itself effect a disposal requiring consent.
There is no minimum holding period, no speculative or short-term trading ban and no LIFO or intention test. The only temporal constraint is that a consent lapses 10 trading days after notification.

clearance.approver: Fletcher Building Limited Company Secretary; delegated to the Deputy Company Secretary if the Company Secretary is not available
clearance.post_trade_to: NZX and ASX, by those persons who have been advised that they are required to make securities trading disclosures
clearance.section: 5.1-5.4; Request for Consent to Trade in Listed Securities form
clearance.evidence: A consent is only valid for a period of 10 trading days after notification.  A consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of material information prior to trading.

exceptions.evidence: Any interest in securities in the Company acquired on accepting an offer under a Company employee share scheme, and the subsequent transfer of the full and unrestricted titles to the shares on the satisfaction of, and at a time fixed by, the terms of the scheme.

Any interest in securities in the Company acquired on participating in the Executive Long-Term Share Scheme or similar legacy schemes; any forfeiture of securities on the failure to meet the performance requirements prescribed; and any transfer of full and unrestricted title at the time fixed by the terms of scheme.
Any shares acquired pursuant to the Company's dividend reinvestment plan.

Any pro-rata offer to all eligible shareholders of securities of the Company, whether to acquire by way of a rights or bonus issues or dispose of through a share repurchase/buy back or general share cancellation plan.
Accepting an offer made to all shareholders pursuant to the New Zealand Takeovers Code.

The excluded transactions are the request to convert any capital notes on an interest re-set date into shares of the Company; any shares so issued; and the repurchase or redemption of the capital note for cash if the company so elects not to issue shares.

external_documents: Fletcher Building Code of Conduct (incorporated into the terms of employment)
Fletcher Building Corporate Governance practices, approved by the board annually
Executive Long-Term Share Scheme (and similar legacy schemes) rules
exemption_authority: No formal exemption or waiver power. The Company Secretary has an unfettered discretion to grant or refuse consent to trade ('the approval to trade is at the discretion of the Fletcher Building Company Secretary'), and Schedule II is expressed as guidance only, so the Company Secretary can in principle consent during a listed No Trade Period. The clause 6 ban on limiting the economic risk of equity incentive remuneration is absolute and has no waiver route. The Board approves the Policy.
jurisdiction_overlays: New Zealand Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 insider trading regime is the primary legal overlay, not the Corporations Act
Dual listed NZX (FBU) and ASX (FBU); designated persons must make securities trading disclosures to both NZX and ASX
New Zealand Takeovers Code (specific insider trading exemption relied on for the takeover carve-out)
Policy expressly contemplates conduct outside New Zealand: 'even conduct that occurs entirely outside of New Zealand can also be subject to New Zealand's insider trading legislation'

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any employee who is offered participation in equity based incentive remuneration is prohibited from entering into transactions (whether through the use of derivatives or otherwise) which limit the economic risk of participating in the equity based incentive remuneration.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only absolute prohibition in the Policy; it is drafted around the incentive remuneration itself rather than around a class of securities, so a collar over shares that are traceably incentive awards still at risk is banned outright with no consent route, while a collar over freely held or fully vested shares is not.

bespoke_clauses.clause: so that the incentive remains at risk until achieved
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This purpose statement is the best argument that the clause 6 ban falls away once awards have vested and unrestricted title has transferred, which is the state in which the bank's collar would be written.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, charges, pledges, encumbrances or forced sales anywhere in its eight clauses or two Schedules.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is unregulated by this Policy, which is unusually permissive by ASX standards; only the derivative legs need clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: To be transacted: On NZX/ASX/off-market trade/other (specify)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The consent form expressly accommodates an off-market trade, confirming that an OTC collar can be described to and consented by the Company Secretary rather than being incapable of clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Fletcher Building securities covered by this Policy include shares, capital notes, options and rights ... and any listed derivatives, including futures contracts or warrants listed on an authorised futures exchange, in respect of Fletcher Building securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Paragraph 3.4 arguably confines 'securities' to listed derivatives while the definition of 'trade' in 1.1 has no venue limit; the conservative reading (consent required for an OTC collar) should be applied, and the ambiguity should be resolved with the Company Secretary in writing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A consent is only valid for a period of 10 trading days after notification.  A consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of material information prior to trading.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The 10 trading day window is generous by ASX standards and allows time to price and document a collar, but the consent self-destructs if the executive learns material information before execution, so a bank should require a bring-down confirmation at signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Although the approval to trade is at the discretion of the Fletcher Building Company Secretary, Schedule II to this Policy sets out some general guidelines on when approval will not be granted.  In declining any approval to trade, no reasons need be given.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Consent can be refused without reasons for any reason, so neither the executive nor the bank can rely on a collar being renewable, rollable or unwindable at a future date.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any significant acquisition or divestment, having regard to the group as a whole: From day that there is a realistic prospect of a transaction arising until after full public disclosure is generally available to the market.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Undisclosed corporate-activity and capital-raising blackouts can arise at any time and are not calendar-bound, so physical settlement, unwind or roll of the collar may be blocked without warning.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any such person is included with respect to all of their interests in any of the Company's securities, whether direct, indirect, contingent, beneficial or legal.  The nature of an interest should be interpreted widely.  This will extend to interests held through other entities or persons (eg trusts, associates, related parties, spouses, and closely-held companies, etc) where the person has the ability to influence or control that person or entity.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A 'contingent' interest is expressly captured, so a collar or loan documented through a family trust or holding company is within the Policy and cannot be used to sidestep the consent requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no minimum holding period, speculative trading ban or intention test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no tenor constraint on a collar and no risk that a short-dated or early-terminating structure is characterised as prohibited short-term dealing.

summary: A funded collar over fully vested, unrestricted Fletcher Building shares is achievable, and this is one of the more permissive policies of its kind. The Policy is silent on margin lending, secured financing, charges and forced sales, so the loan leg secured on the collared shares is not prohibited; the put and call legs are caught only as a 'trade' under paragraph 1.1, which expressly includes trading in derivatives over or relating to Fletcher Building securities with no venue limit. The conditions are prior written notification to and consent from the Company Secretary using the prescribed form (which contemplates an off-market trade), execution within the 10 trading day validity, no material information at execution, and timing outside the 1 July and 1 January No Trade Periods and any undisclosed capital-raising or corporate-activity blackout. The decisive constraint is clause 6: any employee offered equity based incentive remuneration is absolutely prohibited, with no consent route, from any transaction limiting the economic risk of that incentive remuneration, so the collar must be confined to shares whose incentive has been 'achieved' - vested with full and unrestricted title transferred - and must not reach awards still subject to performance hurdles or restriction. Consent is discretionary and may be refused without reasons, so neither entry nor any later roll or unwind can be treated as assured.
